prompt: Review browser security for an analytics SPA hosted at app.example.com that calls api.example.com and loads customer-configured report data from reports.example.net. The API currently reflects the Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and allows credentials; the SPA stores an access token in localStorage; a URL hash controls which report endpoint the client fetches; and the page can be framed by any origin. Redesign CORS for exact required origins and credentials, prevent client-side forged requests from attacker-controlled URL input, choose a safer browser credential/session architecture, constrain framing and navigation, and add CSP/reporting plus explicit XSS-safe rendering rules for report data. Keep OAuth token issuance/validation in oauth-oidc and application API authorization in authorization-security.

requirements: SPA/API/report origins with credentialed and uncredentialed request fixtures
attacker-controlled URL hash and report-content corpus
browser storage and server/BFF session alternatives

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Credentialed CORS is limited to the exact required trusted origins, methods, and headers; the design does not reflect arbitrary Origin values or combine credential sharing with wildcard origin access.

Attacker-controlled URL/hash input cannot cause the trusted SPA to construct an arbitrary privileged API/report request while automatically adding the application's own credentials or anti-CSRF headers.

The credential architecture explicitly weighs JavaScript-readable browser storage exposure and selects a server/BFF or other storage model consistent with the app threat model rather than treating localStorage as inherently safe.
The application uses CSP `frame-ancestors` or an equivalent explicit framing policy so arbitrary sites cannot embed the authenticated UI.
Customer report data reaches only safe rendering sinks or an explicit sanitization boundary, and CSP/reporting is used as defense in depth rather than a substitute for sink safety.
